title: Large NHC track and wind errors occurred together less than an independent reference at 48 hours in the Atlantic in 2019-2025
abstract: We tested whether large official NHC track and absolute wind errors occur together more often than independent errors with the same test-year fractions. Thresholds used the past five years only. In 2019-2025 at 48 hours, 19 of 1,605 Atlantic cycles had both errors above their past 80th percentiles (1.18%, versus 1.98% under independence). The difference was -0.79 percentage points, with 95% whole-storm limits of -1.45 to -0.06 and whole-year limits of -1.21 to -0.31. In 1,087 East Pacific cycles, the joint fraction was 3.40%, versus 3.34%; limits included zero. An exact within-storm and between-storm separation gave uncertain individual terms. Atlantic results changed with threshold and era, so the deficit is not a general law. A chronological direct joint-probability estimate gave no clear score gain across both storm and year uncertainty checks or both basins. We provide code, aggregate results, source hashes and an independent arithmetic check. This is a test of point forecast errors, not of issued joint probabilities. Revised records, excluded stages, sparse joint events, fixed training thresholds, only seven test years and unadjusted comparisons limit inference.

display.caption: Joint large errors and their exact within-storm and between-storm separation. Thresholds use five earlier years. These are error diagnostics, not issued NHC probabilities.
